paper.title: 基于短周期价量特征的多因子选股体系
paper.source: 国泰君安证券研究 / 数量化专题之九十三

scope.purpose: Golden extraction benchmark for all 191 short-cycle price-volume alpha factor definitions and paper-level reproduction method, not a final numeric reproduction proof.
notes: Formula definitions are source-grounded to Table 6 and Appendix 2 of the paper.
Because Table 6 extraction is noisy in PDF text, factor formulas include audit status and should be visually reviewed before being treated as final.

global_method.factor_construction_universe: All A-share stocks with daily price-volume data.
global_method.factor_evaluation_target: Style-neutral alpha return, not raw stock return.

formula_evidence.description: Definitions of variables, functions, and operators used in Table 6.
Single-factor significance, correlation, and effective prediction horizon methodology.

known_limitations: The paper reports aggregate factor-system statistics, but does not provide per-factor numeric evaluation results for all 191 factors.
Table 6 formulas are available in the PDF, but text extraction splits and corrupts some formulas; each formula should be visually audited or cross-checked before finalizing.
The paper reports daily model IC and 30-day IC curves as charts, but not machine-readable per-date IC series.
The paper describes factor/style neutralization methodology, but does not provide daily residualized factor exposures.

variables.BANCHMARKINDEXCLOSE: Benchmark index close; spelling follows the paper.
variables.BANCHMARKINDEXOPEN: Benchmark index open; spelling follows the paper.
variables.SELF: Special recursive variable used in Alpha143; refers to prior-day Alpha143 value.

derived_variables.TR: MAX(MAX(HIGH - LOW, ABS(HIGH - DELAY(CLOSE, 1))), ABS(LOW - DELAY(CLOSE, 1)))

functions.RANK(A): Cross-sectional ascending rank of vector A.
functions.STD(A, n): Time-series standard deviation of A over the past n periods.
functions.CORR(A, B, n): Time-series correlation of A and B over the past n periods.
functions.SUM(A, n): Time-series sum of A over the past n periods.
functions.MEAN(A, n): Time-series mean of A over the past n periods.
functions.TSRANK(A, n): Rank of the latest value of A within the past n periods.
functions.SIGN(A): 1 if A > 0, 0 if A = 0, -1 if A < 0.
functions.COVIANCE(A, B, n): Time-series covariance of A and B over the past n periods; spelling follows the paper.
functions.TSMIN(A, n): Time-series minimum of A over the past n periods.
functions.TSMAX(A, n): Time-series maximum of A over the past n periods.
functions.PROD(A, n): Time-series product of A over the past n periods.
functions.COUNT(condition, n): Count of observations satisfying condition over the past n periods.
functions.REGBETA(A, B, n): Regression beta from regressing A on B over the past n periods.
functions.REGRESI(A, B, n): Regression residual from regressing A on B over the past n periods.
functions.SMA(A, n, m): Recursive moving average: Y_i = (A_i * m + Y_{i-1} * (n - m)) / n.
functions.SUMIF(A, n, condition): Conditional sum of A over the past n periods where condition is true.
functions.WMA(A, n): Weighted moving average over the past n periods with weights 0.9^i.
functions.DECAYLINEAR(A, d): Linear-decay moving average of A with weights d, d-1, ..., 1.
functions.FILTER(A, condition): Filter A to samples satisfying condition.
functions.HIGHDAY(A, n): Number of periods since the maximum value of A within the past n periods.
functions.LOWDAY(A, n): Number of periods since the minimum value of A within the past n periods.
functions.SUMAC(A, n): Cumulative sum of A over the past n periods.

operators.A ? B : C: If A is true, return B; otherwise return C.

notes: Function and variable spelling preserves the paper, including BANCHMARKINDEX and COVIANCE.
LOWDAY is interpreted as periods since the minimum, despite the extracted table text saying maximum; this is inferred from the function name and common GTJA/Alpha operator usage.

raw_formula_value.description: Raw Alpha1-Alpha191 formula value computed from daily price-volume inputs and Table 15 operators.

style_industry_orthogonalized_factor.description: Transform used for single-factor testing and model prediction: orthogonalize each target factor against industry and style factors, then use the residual cross-section.

steps.name: orthogonalization
steps.formula: X_K_t = beta_industry * X_industry + beta_style * X_style + epsilon_K_t

factor_return_regression.description: Regression transform used to estimate a single factor factor return for a given prediction horizon after style and industry controls.

steps.name: future_return_regression
steps.formula: R_{t+d} = f_industry * X_industry + f_style * X_style + f_k * epsilon_K_t + epsilon_{t+d}

alpha_model_prediction.description: Transform used to combine all 191 residualized factors into a predicted next-period alpha return cross-section.

steps.name: factor_return_estimation
steps.formula: R = f_industry * X_industry + f_style * X_style + sum_k(f_k * epsilon_k) + epsilon

single_factor_horizon_test.description: Single-factor significance and effective-horizon test after style and industry orthogonalization.

factor_return_correlation_screen.description: Correlation screen over factor return series after all candidate factors are constructed; if two factors have factor-return correlation above a threshold, retain the factor with higher factor-return IR.

default_spec.screening_rule: when pairwise correlation exceeds threshold xi, remove the lower-IR factor

alpha_model_prediction_ic.description: Prediction test for the full 191-factor alpha model: compare predicted alpha-return cross-section with realized alpha-return cross-section.

factor_count_prediction_ic.description: Model prediction test using top-N factors ranked by single-factor Factor Return IR.

truth_source_rules: Each Alpha formula should be sourced to Table 6.
Rows marked needs_review should be visually audited before strict formula matching is enforced.
Do not include strategy/backtest metrics in this golden file unless the scope is explicitly expanded.
